title: Generic Type-System Troubleshooting
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of generic type-system troubleshooting using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates generic type-system troubleshooting.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Generic Type-System Troubleshooting** as part of **Generics and Type-System Design**. Generics preserve relationships between types and reduce unsafe casts; type constraints and variance should be as simple as the API requires. Use the subtopics—Variance Errors, Type Inference Failures, Simplifying Complex Generic Signatures—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

items.title: Type Inference Failures
items.text: Type Inference Failures helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Generic Type-System Troubleshooting removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
